decision.summary: Two regions warrant closer inspection: (1) a multi-sample, cross-axis divergent trend between indices 480–544 with partial recovery in U but not N/E; (2) a sharp, coherent multi-axis offset beginning at index 725 and persisting to 729, with no return observed. Other intervals show typical noise or smooth motion.

regions.observation: Cross-axis shape: N and E components show correlated multi-sample downward trend from ~index 480 to 520, with U component exhibiting a sharper, earlier drop (~490–505) followed by partial recovery; the three axes do not share a single coherent platform or return, suggesting superposed or non-rigid motion. Region includes the onset of this complex change and its immediate aftermath.

Cross-axis shape: From ~725 onward, all three components (N, E, U) show abrupt, sustained linear trends over just 5 samples—N drops ~1.6 MAD, E rises ~1.8 MAD, U drops ~0.8 MAD—forming a clear multi-axis offset without apparent return within the window. The coherence across axes and sharpness suggest a possible permanent jump or rapid transient event; surroundings (720–724) show relatively stable noise, highlighting the abruptness.
